english.title: Impersonate an enforcement officer under the Property Misdescriptions Act 1991
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), not being a duly authorised officer of an enforcement authority, purported to act as such under the Schedule to the Property Misdescriptions Act 1991
english.legislation: Contrary to paragraph 6 of the Schedule to the Property Misdescriptions Act 1991.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location

investigatoraction.description: Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Section 5 of the Property Misdescriptions Act 1991 provides that the time limit on prosecutions is three years beginning with the date of commission of the offence or the end of the period of one year beginning with the date of the discovery of the offence by the prosecutor, whichever is the earlier.

SUMMARY: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: A fine

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see legislation

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
